en: to become fierce; to turn wild

examples.en: When the wind blows, the waves get rougher and rougher.
When a stranger came, the puppy became fierce.

examples.ko: 배가 고프면 고양이가 사나워질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Cats sometimes get fierce when they are hungry.
The child burst into tears at the angry look on his face.
The weather turned rough, so the plane left late.

examples.ko: 화가 나면 말투가 사나워지는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people's way of speaking becomes harsh when they are angry.

explain: '사납다'는 ㅂ 불규칙이라서 '사나워요', '사나운 개'처럼 바뀌어요. 짐승, 날씨, 표정, 말투에 두루 쓰고, 반의어는 '순하다'예요. '거칠어지다'는 피부나 말처럼 부드럽지 않게 된다는 느낌이라 쓰임이 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: That dog is very fierce.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사나워지다'의 바탕이 되는 형용사로, 이미 사나운 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective behind 사나워지다, describing a state that is already fierce.

phrases.en: They say the weather will turn rough in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이나 비가 거세질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when wind or rain gets rougher.

phrases.en: When he got angry, his expression turned fierce.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 얼굴이나 표정이 무섭게 변할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person's face or expression turns scary.

explain_en: '사납다' is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it changes to '사나워요' and '사나운 개'. It is used for animals, weather, facial expressions and tone of voice, and its opposite is '순하다' (gentle). '거칠어지다' means becoming rough or not smooth, like skin or speech, so the use is a little different.

examples.ko: 이 색은 너무 옅어서 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: This color is so light that the letters are hard to see.

examples.ko: 물을 너무 많이 넣어서 물감 색이 옅어요.
examples.en: I added too much water, so the paint color is pale.
I bought a pale sky-blue T-shirt.
You look natural because you wore light makeup.
The fog has become much thinner than in the morning.

examples.ko: 향이 옅을 때는 한 번 더 뿌려요.
examples.en: When the scent is faint, I spray it once more.

explain: 색, 냄새, 안개처럼 진한 정도를 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '짙다'예요. 묽은 커피나 차는 '연하다'를 더 자주 써요. 말할 때는 받침 소리가 달라져서 [엳따]로 읽어요.

phrases.en: I like light blue clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸미는 '-ㄴ' 모양이에요. 색을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form that describes the noun after it, often used for colors.

phrases.en: The fog thinned out in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-어지다'를 붙여 점점 변하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-어지다' shows that something gradually changes.

phrases.en: I painted the colors lightly in the picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 어떻게 하는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-게' shows how the action is done.

explain_en: It describes how faint a color, smell, or fog is. Its opposite is 짙다. For weak coffee or tea, 연하다 is more common. It is pronounced [엳따].

examples.en: The baby's skin is milky white, so it's really pretty.

examples.ko: 아침 안개 속에서 호수가 우윳빛으로 보였어요.
examples.en: In the morning fog the lake looked milky white.
I bought a milky white ceramic cup.
That actor is famous for milky white skin.
The winter morning sky is hazy, like milk.
This paint is a white close to milky white.

explain: 순백이 아니라 약간 부드럽고 탁한 흰색을 말할 때 써요. 피부를 칭찬할 때 '우윳빛 피부'라고 많이 해요. '분홍빛'처럼 '빛'이 붙는 색 표현 중 하나예요.

phrases.en: I envy her milky-white skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 희고 부드러운 피부를 칭찬할 때 가장 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for praising soft, fair skin.

phrases.en: A milky-white fog settled in this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안개나 구름이 뿌옇게 하얗게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fog or cloud looks hazy white.

phrases.en: The water turned milky white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 맑았던 것이 뿌옇게 흰색이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something clear becomes cloudy white.

explain_en: It describes a soft, slightly opaque white rather than pure white. People often praise skin as '우윳빛 피부'. It is one of the '-빛' color words, like '분홍빛'.

examples.ko: 동생은 화가 나면 말끝이 짧아지고 목소리가 높아져요.
examples.en: When my younger sibling is angry, their sentences get clipped and their voice gets higher.
When winter comes, the days gradually get shorter.
I got a haircut and my hair got a lot shorter.
I washed the pants and it seems the length got shorter.

examples.ko: 방학이 짧아지면 여행 계획도 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: If the vacation gets shorter, we have to change our travel plans too.

examples.ko: 시간이 부족해서 회의가 짧아질 것 같아요.
examples.en: We're short on time, so the meeting will probably be shorter.

explain: 반대말은 '길어지다'예요. 길이뿐 아니라 시간, 말, 글이 줄어들 때도 써요. '줄어들다'는 양이나 수가 적어질 때 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I got a haircut, so my hair is much shorter now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변화가 끝난 결과를 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form describes the result of a finished change.

phrases.en: If your hair gets shorter, it'll feel cooler.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건을 말할 때 '-면'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-면' to state a condition.

phrases.en: The meeting time got shorter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이에요. 양이나 수가 적어질 때 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word; fits better when amount or number decreases.

explain_en: Becomes shorter by itself, like daylight or hair length. The opposite is '길어지다'. It is used for length, but also when time, speech or writing gets shorter. '줄어들다' fits better when an amount or number decreases.

t90.ax: I got a haircut and my hair got a lot shorter.

examples.en: After playing in the winter sea, my lips turned blue.
In autumn the sky is clear, so it gets bluer.
I saw his face turn pale blue from shock.
I played in the pool until my lips turned blue.

examples.ko: 물감을 더 넣으면 색이 파래질 거예요.
examples.en: If you add more paint, the color will turn bluer.

examples.ko: 오래 밖에 있었더니 손가락이 파래지고 아팠어요.
examples.en: After being outside for a long time, my fingers turned blue and hurt.

explain: '파랗다'에 '-아지다'가 붙은 말이라 '파래져요'로 활용해요. 추위나 놀람 때문에 입술·얼굴이 파랗게 변할 때 자주 쓰고, 놀라서 얼굴색이 변하는 건 '파랗게 질리다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: It was so cold that my lips turned blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추위 때문에 몸 색이 변할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when the body changes color because of cold.

phrases.example: 큰 소리에 놀라서 얼굴이 파랗게 질렸어요.
phrases.en: My face went pale from the loud noise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 무서워서 얼굴색이 변할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's face loses color from shock or fear.

phrases.en: After the rain stops, the sky gradually turns blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 파란색이 되어 가는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a gradual change toward blue.

explain_en: It is '파랗다' plus '-아지다', so it conjugates as '파래져요'. It is often used when lips or a face turn blue from cold or shock, and a face going pale from fright can also be described with '파랗게 질리다'.

examples.en: The spot where I bumped turned a deep bluish bruise.
I got a blue bruise on my knee.
The mold was bluish-green, so I threw the bread away.

examples.ko: 멍 색이 이제 덜 퍼레 보여요.
examples.en: The bruise looks less blue now.
The deep blue bruise turned yellow after a few days.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 입술이 퍼레요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day, and my lips are blue.

explain: '파랗다'보다 짙고 탁한 파란색이에요. 그래서 멍이나 추위로 변한 입술처럼 좋지 않은 느낌에 자주 써요. '시퍼렇다'는 더 강한 말이고, 활용은 '퍼레요'처럼 ㅎ이 빠져요.

phrases.en: I fell and got a deep blue bruise on my leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 'ㅎ'이 빠져 '퍼런'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, the ㅎ drops and it becomes '퍼런'.

phrases.en: My lips are blue from the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-어요'가 붙으면 'ㅎ'이 빠지고 '퍼레요'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: When '-어요' is added, the ㅎ drops and it becomes '퍼레요'.

phrases.en: The arm I bumped turned a very deep blue with a bruise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '퍼렇게'보다 색이 더 강하고 진할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the color is stronger and deeper than with '퍼렇게'.

explain_en: It is a deeper, duller blue than '파랗다', so it is often used for unpleasant things like bruises or lips discolored by cold. '시퍼렇다' is the stronger form, and it conjugates by dropping ㅎ, as in '퍼레요'.

en: to be strenuous; to be laborious

examples.en: I have a lot of work, so things have gotten much harder lately.
Exercising outside gets harder in winter.
As the exam gets closer, studying will get harder.
I didn't give up even as the situation got harder and harder.
Breathing got hard when I climbed the stairs, so I rested.
What if getting to work gets harder after we move?

explain: '힘들다'는 지금의 상태이고, '힘들어지다'는 그 상태로 변해 가는 것이에요. 몸이 지치는 것뿐 아니라 마음이나 상황이 부담스러워질 때도 써요. 반대로 쉬워지면 '편해지다'나 '쉬워지다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Work will get harder from tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 더 힘든 상태가 될 것이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say things will become harder from now on.

phrases.en: Please take a rest before it gets too hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 전에'와 함께 힘든 상태가 되기 전의 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-기 전에', it talks about what to do before things get hard.

phrases.en: Studying has gotten a lot harder lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가까운 사람에게 말하는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for friends and close people.

explain_en: '힘들다' is the current state; '힘들어지다' is turning into that state. It covers not only a tired body but also a mind or situation becoming a burden. When things ease up, use '편해지다' or '쉬워지다'.

examples.en: The winter wind was so biting that my ears turned red.
I walked for a long time in the winter wind.

examples.ko: 오늘은 겨울바람 때문에 더 춥게 느껴져요.
examples.en: It feels even colder today because of the winter wind.

examples.ko: 겨울바람이 불면 따뜻한 국물이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: When the winter wind blows, I crave something with warm broth.
I packed a scarf and gloves to stand up to the winter wind.

examples.ko: 창문 틈으로 겨울바람이 들어와서 방이 추워요.
examples.en: Winter wind comes in through the gap in the window, so the room is cold.

explain: 바람이 '불다', 바람을 '맞다'와 자주 같이 써요. 같은 느낌으로 '찬바람'이라고도 하는데, 이건 겨울이 아니어도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: A cold wind was blowing, so I wore a scarf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절과 상관없이 차가운 바람을 말하고, 겨울바람보다 쓰는 범위가 넓어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means any cold wind regardless of season, so it is broader than 겨울바람.

phrases.en: The winter wind is blowing hard today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 부는 모습을 말할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for describing wind blowing.

phrases.en: The winter wind was cold, so I put on gloves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람의 차가운 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how cold the wind feels.

explain_en: It pairs naturally with 바람이 불다 (the wind blows) and 바람을 맞다 (to be hit by wind). '찬바람' (cold wind) is similar but can be used outside winter too.

examples.en: The rose blossoms in the garden are in full bloom.

examples.ko: 꽃송이 하나를 꺾어서 책 사이에 끼웠어요.
examples.en: I picked one blossom and tucked it between the pages of a book.
A sunflower blossom is as big as a face.

examples.ko: 꽃송이마다 벌이 한 마리씩 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A bee is sitting on each blossom.

examples.ko: 꽃송이를 몇 개만 골라 화병에 꽂았어요.
examples.en: I picked just a few blossoms and put them in a vase.
Big snowflakes are pouring down like blossoms outside the window.

explain: 줄기에 달린 꽃 한 덩이를 말해요. '꽃 한 송이'처럼 세는 단위 '송이'가 붙은 말이에요. '꽃'은 식물 전체를 가리킬 때도 있지만 '꽃송이'는 달려 있는 꽃의 덩어리를 말해요.

phrases.en: I bought one rose.
phrases.nuance_ko: '송이'는 꽃을 세는 단위예요. 숫자와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '송이' is the counter for flowers, used with numbers.

phrases.en: This flower has a very big bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃 한 덩이의 크기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the size of a single bloom.

phrases.example: 봄이 되면 나무에 꽃송이가 많이 달려요.
phrases.en: In spring, many blossoms hang on the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무나 줄기에 꽃이 많이 붙어 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes many blossoms attached to a tree or stem.

explain_en: It means one bloom on a stem, built on the counter '송이' as in '꽃 한 송이'. '꽃' can refer to the plant in general, but '꽃송이' points to the flower head itself.

t90.ax: A bee is sitting on each blossom.

examples.ko: 독해력을 키우려면 매일 조금씩 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To build reading comprehension, you have to read a little every day.
Reading comprehension makes a difference in exam scores.

examples.ko: 독해력이 부족하면 긴 글이 어렵게 느껴져요.
examples.en: If your reading comprehension is weak, long texts feel hard.

examples.ko: 독해력 문제는 시간이 모자라서 다 못 풀었어요.
examples.en: I ran out of time and couldn't finish the reading section.
Compared to my Korean reading, my speaking is weak.
Reading comprehension also definitely improves with practice.

explain: '독해력이 좋다/부족하다', '독해력을 키우다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 요즘은 글을 읽고 이해하는 힘을 '문해력'이라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I read a lot, so my reading comprehension is good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 잘 이해한다고 칭찬하거나 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone understands texts well.

phrases.en: My reading comprehension is weak, so long texts are hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '좋다'의 반대로 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 좋다.

phrases.en: They say literacy is important these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '독해력'과 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 요즘 더 많이 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 독해력 but heard more often in everyday talk these days.

explain_en: Skill of understanding written text (독해력 향상) It goes with '독해력이 좋다/부족하다' and '독해력을 키우다'. These days people also often say '문해력' for the ability to read and understand text.

examples.ko: 봄꽃이 피기 시작해서 공원에 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Spring flowers have started to bloom, so the park is crowded.
I went to the spring flower festival with my family.
Forsythia and azaleas are typical spring flowers.

examples.ko: 갑자기 추워져서 올해 봄꽃은 늦게 필 것 같아요.
examples.en: It suddenly got cold, so the spring flowers will probably bloom late this year.

examples.ko: 봄꽃 구경하러 이번 주말에 어디로 갈까요?
examples.en: Where should we go this weekend to see spring flowers?

examples.ko: 비가 오면 봄꽃이 금방 떨어져서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: When it rains, the spring flowers fall quickly, which is a pity.

explain: 벚꽃, 개나리, 진달래처럼 봄에 피는 꽃을 모두 가리켜요. 꽃을 보러 가는 일은 '꽃구경'이나 '꽃놀이'라고 해요.

phrases.en: When the weather gets warm, spring flowers bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄꽃이 활짝 열리는 모습을 말할 때 '피다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 피다 for spring flowers blooming.

phrases.en: Shall we go to see the flowers this weekend?
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄꽃을 보러 가는 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for going out to see spring flowers.

phrases.en: I took a lot of spring flower photos in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄꽃을 찍은 사진을 말할 때 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before 사진 for photos of spring flowers.

explain_en: It covers all flowers that bloom in spring, such as cherry blossoms, forsythia and azaleas. Going out to see flowers is called '꽃구경' or '꽃놀이'.

examples.en: In autumn the leaves on the trees turn yellow.
When the wind blew, the leaves shook.

examples.ko: 큰 잎사귀 하나를 주워서 책에 끼웠어요.
examples.en: I picked up one big leaf and put it in a book.
Morning dew has formed on the leaf.

examples.ko: 이 화분은 잎사귀는 크지만 꽃은 작아요.
examples.en: This pot has big leaves but small flowers.
The rabbit ate the leaves happily.

explain: '잎'과 같은 뜻으로 써요. 나무에 달린 잎은 '나뭇잎', 풀의 잎은 '풀잎'이라고도 해요. 떨어진 잎은 '낙엽'이라고 하고, 잎사귀는 잎 하나하나를 말하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: New leaves have come out on the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잎사귀'와 같은 뜻이고 더 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 잎사귀, but shorter.

phrases.en: Many leaves have fallen on the ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무에서 나온 잎을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to be clear it's a leaf from a tree.

phrases.en: When the wind blew, the leaves fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잎이 나무에서 내려오는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe leaves falling from a tree.

explain_en: Longer form for one leaf, softer feel (잎사귀 하나) It means the same as '잎'. A leaf on a tree is a '나뭇잎' and a leaf of grass is a '풀잎'. A fallen leaf is a '낙엽', and 잎사귀 has the feel of one leaf at a time.

t90.ax: The rabbit ate the leaves happily.
